_comment: Human-curated backlog of real, searched HVAC problems. The daily generator works through these top-to-bottom, skipping any already published or parked in content-rejected.json. Order = priority: furnace fault codes first (heating season), then furnace symptoms, heat pumps, ACs, thermostats, mini splits. Codes come from manufacturer LED/display tables (Carrier=Bryant boards, Goodman=Amana boards, Trane=American Standard boards; Lennox E-codes; York flash codes); the AI reviewer and the human review PR verify each code's meaning. Entries tagged _source=queue were inserted from real visitor searches.

meaning: Limit Circuit Lockout — the limit or flame rollout switch stayed open for more than 3 minutes; control auto-resets after 3 hours. A tripped rollout switch needs a manual reset.

Ignition Proving Failure — control did not prove flame during a trial for ignition (dirty flame sensor, igniter, gas supply, reversed polarity or poor ground); the control retries, and repeated failures become Code 14.

Limit Circuit Fault — the limit or flame rollout switch opened for less than 3 minutes (restricted airflow: dirty filter, closed registers, blower problem, or overheating); blower runs 4 minutes or until the switch closes. Rollout switch needs a manual reset.
Limit Circuit Lockout — the limit or flame rollout switch stayed open for more than 3 minutes; control auto-resets after 3 hours. A tripped rollout switch needs a manual reset.
Blower On After Power Up — 115 VAC or 24 VAC power was interrupted during a call for heat; blower runs about 90 seconds, then normal operation resumes. A status/history code, not a lockout.
Ignition Lockout — control failed to prove flame in 4 ignition trials, or lost flame 5 times in one heating cycle; auto-resets after 3 hours.

Gas Heating Lockout — control senses the gas valve relay contacts closed (valve energized) when they should be open: a mis-wired gas valve or a shorted gas valve relay/driver on the control board. Does not auto-reset; clears only on a power cycle. Not a gas-supply or ignition problem.

Abnormal Flame-Proving Signal — flame is sensed while the gas valve is de-energized; the inducer runs until flame goes out. Points to a leaking or stuck-open gas valve or residual flame, not to ignition.
Pressure Switch Did Not Open — pressure switch contacts were closed at the start of the heating cycle before the inducer started (stuck-closed switch or shorted switch wiring).

Secondary Voltage Fuse Is Open — the 3 A low-voltage fuse on the control board is blown, almost always from a short in the 24 V thermostat or accessory wiring. The board is unpowered, so the LED may be dark.

Low-Pressure Switch Did Not Close or Reopened — the low-stage pressure switch on two-stage/multi-stage boards (draft/inducer proving), NOT an airflow or limit fault. Legends vary by board; the door-label legend for the unit governs.
Blower Motor Fault — the ECM/variable-speed blower did not start or ran outside its valid speed range (motor, wiring, or motor communication). Variable-speed boards only.
Inducer Motor Fault — the inducer did not start or ran outside its valid speed range (variable-speed / two-stage condensing boards).

Pressure Switch Calibration Fault — on variable-speed condensing boards the inducer could not be calibrated against the low-pressure switch (switch opened or closed at the wrong inducer speed); usually venting, tubing, or the switch.
Blower Calibration Fault — on variable-speed boards the blower motor calibration failed (motor ran outside the expected range during calibration). Not a gas-valve code; legends vary by board.

Control Circuitry Lockout — auto-resets after 1 hour; caused by a flame-sense circuit failure, a software check error, or a stuck gas-valve relay on the control board. If it repeats, the control board is the usual fix.
Blower On After Power Up — 115 VAC or 24 VAC power was interrupted during a call for heat; blower runs about 90 seconds, then normal operation resumes. A status/history code, not a lockout.
Ignition Lockout — control failed to prove flame in 4 ignition trials, or lost flame 5 times in one heating cycle; auto-resets after 3 hours.

Pressure switch stuck closed — the pressure switch circuit was closed before the inducer started (stuck switch or shorted wiring).

Open high-limit switch — the primary limit opened from overheating (dirty filter, restricted airflow, blower problem); resets when the furnace cools.
Flame sensed with no call for heat — flame present when the gas valve should be closed (leaking gas valve, or flame sensor/wiring fault).
